acceptance: A proof matrix maps every concurrency invariant to its producer, consumer, failure injection, test layer, supported platforms, and retained evidence.
Unit tests cover state transitions, synchronization publication order, validation-policy isolation, deterministic generation, metric suppression, and stale-owner fencing.
Integration tests cover phase containment with live outstanding work, multiprocess admission, lease loss, cancellation/publication races, restart, and unknown-outcome recovery.
Adapter UAT proves session identity, concurrent overlap, configuration equivalence, cleanup, and native cancellation only for adapters that claim those capabilities.
Negative controls demonstrate that each test fails when its protected invariant is deliberately violated; timing-only sleeps are not the sole synchronization oracle.

The final report separates repository verification, hosted CI, adapter UAT, and deferred operator-controlled external MCP acceptance; it makes no production-readiness claim without the external runbook evidence.
context: This item is the only convergence point. It must not reopen implementation decisions unless evidence falsifies them; failures return to the owning prerequisite item. External MCP production acceptance stays deferred and operator-owned.
description:
Close the concurrency work with evidence at the boundary each claim depends on. Unit tests alone cannot prove phase isolation, multiprocess lease behavior, real session equivalence, or operator deployment. Build a traceable proof matrix and run the repository-verifiable portions without conflating them with deferred external acceptance.

Decision boundary: a claim passes only at the lowest layer capable of falsifying it. Mock-based success cannot certify real database cancellation or adapter session equivalence, and local MCP tests cannot certify an external production deployment.
